subject: Banking
title: Commercial vs Investment Banks
description: A micro-lesson that makes Commercial vs Investment Banks usable.

hook.text: Your local bank takes deposits and makes loans. An investment bank does neither. It deals in companies, not customers.

buildup.text: Commercial banks earn from the spread between deposit interest and loan interest. Investment banks earn from deal fees.

discovery.text: Investment banks help companies raise money, go public, merge with rivals, or sell divisions. Every service earns a fee.

twist.text: After Glass-Steagall was repealed in 1999, the line blurred.

climax.text: Investment banking is finance for corporations. It moves billions between companies rather than thousands between.

punchline.text: Your bank serves people. Investment banks serve corporations.

quiz.question: How do investment banks primarily earn revenue?
options: Fees from corporate deals like IPOs and mergers
